Entries.Text: Colours the materials, bones, dummies and meshes in Contents that differ from the game's own model (green) or aren't in it (blue). The vanilla model is read once when a model is loaded; Tools › Vanilla Compare lists the differences.

How the loaded model differs from the game's own. Select an object (here, in Contents or in the viewport) to see its fields against vanilla and revert them. Objects are paired by name (dummies by reference ID, meshes by material and vertex count), and indices are compared by the bone or material they point at, so adding or moving objects doesn't make others look changed.
Load a model to compare it with vanilla.
The game has no model {0} (the mod added it), or it couldn't be read.
How many objects each list has here and in vanilla, and how many are modified, added and removed.
The first selected material, bone, dummy or mesh against its vanilla counterpart. Select the model root for the model's own fields (header, buffer layouts, skeleton set).
Select a material, bone, dummy or mesh, or the model root.
Sets this field back to vanilla's value. A bone or material index is set to wherever that bone or material is now. Can be undone.

Puts the mesh's vertices, faces, vertex buffers, bounds and bone table back to vanilla's, with bone and layout indices mapped to this model. The viewport shows it after the next live preview (or Refresh Viewport). Can be undone.
Reverts every field listed above, as one undo step. Fields that can't be reverted are logged.
Every modified and added object (click to select), and the vanilla objects this model no longer has.
Adds the vanilla object back, at the end of its list, with its bones found by name. Can be undone.
Replaces the model with vanilla's. Asks first, as it clears the undo history.

Replace {0} with the game's own model? Every material, bone, dummy and mesh goes back to vanilla, and the undo history is cleared, so this can't be undone. Nothing is written until you save. Cloth and collision files are left as they are.
Leaves the model as it is.
{0} was reverted to vanilla. Save to keep it.
it is only reported here; Revert Model to Vanilla resets it

A removed mesh can't be restored on its own. Revert Model to Vanilla brings every mesh back.
